title: Building Floor Plan 3D Navigator
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive 3D building floor plan navigator with the following specifications:

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera starting at position (0, 25, 30) looking down at the building at angle.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (10, 30, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Set renderer background to #1a1a2e. Enable antialiasing and shadows.
- The building has exactly 5 floors (index 0-4), each floor is a flat slab (20 x 0.3 x 15) stacked vertically with 4 units of vertical spacing between floor centers.
- Floor 0 center Y = 0, Floor 1 center Y = 4, Floor 2 center Y = 8, Floor 3 center Y = 12, Floor 4 center Y = 16.
- Each floor slab is a BoxGeometry colored with a unique color: Floor 0 = #4a90d9, Floor 1 = #50c878, Floor 2 = #f5a623, Floor 3 = #d94a68, Floor 4 = #9b59b6.
- On each floor, place 3-5 room partition walls as thin BoxGeometry objects (height 2.5, thickness 0.15) in different layouts per floor to represent different room configurations. Walls should be #e0e0e0.
- Add small colored cubes (0.5x0.5x0.5) on each floor representing furniture: at least 2 per floor, placed on top of the floor slab.

## Floor Selection & Isolation
- Maintain a currentFloor state (initially -1 meaning 'all floors visible').
- When a specific floor is selected, animate all OTHER floors to become transparent (opacity 0.1) over 500ms, and move the camera to focus on the selected floor. The selected floor and its children (walls, furniture) remain fully opaque (opacity 1.0).
- When currentFloor is -1 (overview mode), all floors are fully opaque and camera returns to the overview position.

## Camera Modes
- Two camera modes: 'orbit' (default) and 'walkthrough'.
- In orbit mode, the user can rotate around the building using OrbitControls. The orbit target should be the center of the selected floor, or (0, 8, 0) in overview mode.
- In walkthrough mode, the camera is placed at Y = selectedFloor * 4 + 1.6 (eye height) on the selected floor, looking forward along -Z. WASD keys move the camera on the XZ plane (speed 0.15 per frame). This mode is only available when a specific floor is selected (currentFloor >= 0).

## Measurement Tool
- A measurement mode toggled by a button. When active, clicking two points on the current floor (via raycasting against the floor slab and walls) places small red spheres (radius 0.15) at those points and draws a line between them. A label (HTML overlay or sprite) shows the distance in meters (1 unit = 1 meter) rounded to 2 decimal places.
- Store the last measurement distance in state. Maximum of one active measurement at a time (new measurement replaces old).

## Floor Area Calculation
- Each floor has a computed total area of 20 * 15 = 300 square meters. Display this in the HUD when a floor is selected.

## DOM UI / HUD
- A panel on the left side with:
  - Title: 'Floor Navigator'
  - 6 buttons: 'Overview' (sets currentFloor=-1), 'Floor 0' through 'Floor 4' (sets currentFloor to 0-4). Active button should be visually highlighted.
  - A 'Camera Mode' toggle button showing current mode ('Orbit' / 'Walkthrough').
  - A 'Measure' toggle button.
- A top-right HUD overlay showing:
  - Current floor label (or 'All Floors')
  - Camera mode
  - Floor area (when a floor is selected): '300.00 m²'
  - Last measurement distance (if any): 'Distance: X.XX m'

## State Management (CRITICAL)
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- currentFloor: number (-1 for overview, 0-4 for specific floor)
- cameraMode: string ('orbit' | 'walkthrough')
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z} — current camera world position
- floorCount: number (always 5)
- floorOpacities: array of 5 numbers (each floor's current opacity, 0.0-1.0)
- selectedFloorArea: number (300 when a floor is selected, 0 in overview)
- measurementActive: boolean
- measurementDistance: number|null (distance of last measurement, or null)
- measurementPoints: number (0, 1, or 2 — how many points placed)
- walkthroughPosition: {x, y, z} | null (camera position in walkthrough mode, null otherwise)
- roomCount: array of 5 numbers (number of room partitions per floor)
- furnitureCount: array of 5 numbers (number of furniture items per floor)
- totalObjects: number (total mesh count in scene)
- animating: boolean (true during floor transition animations)

Ensure all numerical values are never NaN or Infinity. Update state every animation frame.
physics_constraints: Floor slabs must be positioned at exact Y intervals of 4 units (Y = 0, 4, 8, 12, 16). Camera in walkthrough mode must stay at eye height Y = floor*4 + 1.6 and be constrained to XZ bounds of the floor slab (-10 to 10 on X, -7.5 to 7.5 on Z). Opacity transitions must interpolate smoothly from current value to target over 500ms. Measurement distances must be Euclidean and NaN-free. Floor area is always exactly 300.00 m² per floor.
